That measurement is false, by the route's own logs and by independent reproduction. It is the sole empirical support for the claim that the remaining architecture is empty at the sizes tested.

findings.result_name: lane:budget (listed as "proved" in the results array; headline: "lane:exit-chain closes the single-driver two-phase lane by a delay+reach<=k+1 budget")
findings.defect: Only lane:exit-chain is proved. The two-phase lane family is never defined in the deliverable (no masses, no rewards, no driver constant), so neither of the two claims it rests on can be checked, and no argument in the route bounds the TOTAL run length by delay+reach — delay+reach <= k+1 bounds one epoch, not a run that could have many epochs. GAP: "For the two-phase lane of lane:budget, every all-switches run has length at most k+O(1)" is asserted, not proved.
findings.evidence: In the paste-ready LaTeX lane:budget is a \begin{remark}; its clause (i) ("the driver cannot fire before round k-j+1, because until then val(l_j) has not moved") and clause (ii) ("the exit wave ... can never reach l_j, so it makes at most j-1 switches") are stated without proof about a family given only in prose. lane:exit-chain itself I reconstructed and it is correct: W = {d, l_1..l_j} with pi_a is a closed configuration in the sense of frontier's definition preceding prop:closed-now-or-never ("every vertex reachable from pi(W) by a path whose interior avoids W is an average vertex, a member of W, or a sink"), W_t = {d} is nonempty and misses S_{sigma_t}, so prop:closed-now-or-never(b) applies. But (ii) additionally needs "the exit wave leaves l_1..l_{j-1} at exit while it reaches l_j", which is a design assumption about the undefined family, and the step from "the all-exit configuration never recurs" to "the run is at most k+O(1) rounds" is not made.

findings.defect: Two random searches are described as "exact scans". findings.defect: The statement writes "Let h := p^{u,b}_u = h(b -> u)", identifying two different quantities: p^{u,b}_u is the probability that the FIRST controlled vertex met after leaving u by b is u itself, while thm:impedance's h(b -> u) is the probability of EVER visiting u. They differ whenever a controlled vertex other than u lies on a return path, which stopping does not forbid (lem:trapchar makes only the subgraph induced on C acyclic; cycles through average vertices are allowed). The proposition's conclusion does not use h, so nothing downstream breaks.
findings.evidence: Explicit stopping counterexample: Vmax = {u,w}, Vavg = {g1,g2}; u -> (t1,g1), g1 -> (w,t0), w -> (g2,t0), g2 -> (u,t0). The greatest trap is empty (g1 loses t0, then g2, then u and w), so the game is stopping. With b = g1: p^{u,1}_u = 0 because the first controlled vertex met from g1 is w with probability 1, while under sigma(w) = g2 the hitting probability h(g1 -> u) = 1/2.

findings.defect: "strictly sharper than thm:peak-law in the direction that matters" is wrong: the two are incomparable. thm:peak-law asserts that the peak is attained on Delta(sigma,sigma') AND that every such peak vertex satisfies val_{sigma'}(sigma(v)) <= val_{sigma'}(sigma'(v)); lane:peak-source gives neither. The proof is also heavier than needed: the same conclusion drops out of thm:peak-law's own proof, since delta <= 0 off S_sigma gives phi <= P phi outside S_sigma and the closedness argument then applies verbatim.

The lower-bound argument given is correct (in a one-player game every value is a sink value or an average-vertex value, so k pairwise distinct exit values force a >= k-2 and hence N >= 2k), but CL(k) has N = 2k+2, two above the bound; nothing rules out or exhibits a lane at N = 2k or 2k+1.

findings.defect: The lemma is the unrolled form of an inequality already established inside the proof of thm:peak-law, and round 14 already recorded the same fact in prose. The route presents it as the new law that refutes the premise the route was opened on, without attributing either.
findings.evidence: thm:peak-law's proof (frontier.tex line ~3490) derives phi <= P phi + delta with delta(v) = x(sigma'(v)) - x(sigma(v)); at a Max vertex not strictly switchable delta(v) <= 0, so phi(v) <= phi(sigma'(v)), and unrolling through the average part (phi is the mean at average vertices, 0 at the sinks) gives (1-p_v) phi(v) <= sum_{w != v} p_w phi(w), which is exactly lane:rise-bound. Round 14's fs14:gap (free-search-14/fs14.tex): "a switch that was non-improving before the trigger gains at most what its option gained, since val_sigma is 1-Lipschitz in a frozen payoff". The lemma itself is correct: I verified it on 61095 (game, sigma, sigma', u) instances over random stopping games with 3-8 non-sinks and both players present, 0 violations.

findings.defect: The hypothesis "one-player SSG" is unnecessarily narrow: the proof needs only U subset of Vmax with W(u,a) contained in U for both a, which forces G|_U to be one-player regardless of whether the ambient game has Min vertices. The route's own verification (610 projections) and mine (5986) were run on TWO-player games, i.e. on a case the stated proposition does not cover.
findings.evidence: For u in U, val_sigma(u) = sum_w p^{u,sigma(u)}_w val_sigma(w) + q with the sum over W(u,sigma(u)) contained in U, so val_sigma|_U solves a system in U alone whose matrix is transient (stopping), hence has a unique solution equal to val^{G|_U}_{sigma|_U}. Verified: t_rise.py, 5986 projected switch sequences over all autonomous U in random two-player stopping games, both (a) once empty always empty and (b) nonempty projections pairwise distinct, 0 violations.

verdict:
NOT SOUND: three major findings survive. The mathematics is in better shape than the reporting. Every result the route marks "proved" I reconstructed and found correct — lane:rise-bound, lane:no-overtake, lane:impedance-cancels, lane:peak-source, lane:autonomy, lane:modules, lane:exit-chain, lane:three/lane:linear, lane:grid, lane:rc-optimal and lane:tree — and I rebuilt every family and instance from the statements in my own exact-arithmetic code (directory /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-lane-reuse-correctness/, manifest in AUDIT.md). RC(k), ALH(k), CL(k) reproduce exactly for k = 2..12 / 2..12 / 2..6, including the CL cube-tie sequence 0,2,12,46,144 and the C(k,2) run ties of RC and ALH; the 15-vertex tree-lag instance reproduces exactly, trace and all; lane:rise-bound, lane:peak-source and lane:autonomy survived 61095 / 2493 / 5986 exact checks on random two-player stopping games with no violation; lane:grid survived 1628 runs. None of the project's standing errors is present: val_sigma is never taken by greedy policy iteration, no dict-literal row collapses, no sink-index collision, the trap for stopping correctly excludes both sinks, no decision rule is claimed so the own-successor rule and the Z_0/Z_1 seed are not in scope, no target-equivalent oracle is assumed, and no terminal round is counted (L is productive rounds throughout).

What fails is the negative side. (1) The route's central empirical claim about the ONE architecture its own theorems leave open — that the mixture-driven turnaround family "found nothing longer than |Vmax|" at k <= 5, repeated four times across the JSON and the LaTeX — is false. Its own rl_k3.log records height 6 at |Vmax| = 5 and rl_k5.log records height 8 at |Vmax| = 7, and I rebuilt the family from the route's own docstring and found an explicit nondegenerate RL(3) normal form of height 6 > 5 (parameters and run printed in verify_rl3.py). (2) lane:budget, listed as proved and headlined as "closing" the single-driver two-phase lane, is a remark about a family the deliverable never defines; lane:exit-chain is proved, but the two clauses that convert it into a k+O(1) bound are asserted, and delay+reach bounds one epoch, not a run. (3) Both scans behind that closure are random searches (200000 independent draws; simulated annealing) described as "exact scans", which is the specific evidential failure the round's rules forbid.

The minor findings are a cluster of degeneracy/Holt-Klee inferences that are wrong but numerically harmless (CL(2) is nondegenerate by the route's own table; a run with no tied incidence is bound by the Holt-Klee ceiling through cor:one-tie, so neither CL nor the m=5 height-8 instance escapes it, and a nondegenerate m=5 height-8 instance exists in the route's own logs anyway), a false identification of the first-passage return mass p^{u,b}_u with thm:impedance's hitting probability h(b->u) (explicit stopping counterexample given; nothing downstream uses it), an off-by-one between announced heights and printed specs in one of the three searches, a graph-level search table that misses the route's own RC(9) and RC(10), an overstated novelty claim for lane:peak-source, and three \Cref labels that do not exist in frontier.tex. The headline "the reopening premise is FALSE and now provably so" is defensible in the precise form the route states in lane:accounting, but the underlying inequality is the unrolled form of a step already inside thm:peak-law's proof and was already recorded in prose in round 14's fs14:gap; neither is attributed.

Recommended disposition: keep lane:rise-bound, lane:peak-source, lane:autonomy/lane:modules, lane:exit-chain, lane:three/lane:linear, lane:grid/lane:rc-optimal and lane:tree (all correct); withdraw the "nothing longer than |Vmax|" measurement and the claim that the mixture architecture is empty at k <= 5, replacing it with the RL(3) height-6 witness; demote lane:budget's conclusion to a GAP with the family written out; and strike the four "the Holt-Klee ceiling does not apply" clauses.
